text_blocks.snippet: Infusion therapy, while often effective, can cause various side effects, ranging from mild to severe. Common side effects include fatigue, nausea, and changes in blood pressure. Some may experience injection site reactions like pain, swelling, or bruising. More serious reactions, though rare, can include allergic reactions (itching, rash, or difficulty breathing), and in very rare cases, anaphylaxis.
snippet_highlighted_words: fatigue, nausea, and changes in blood pressure

list.snippet: Fatigue: It's normal to feel tired after treatment as your body adjusts to the medication.
Nausea and Upset Stomach: Certain therapies can affect the digestive system, causing nausea or stomach upset.
Changes in Blood Pressure: Some treatments may cause low or high blood pressure, potentially leading to dizziness or lightheadedness.
Injection Site Reactions: Pain, swelling, redness, or bruising at the IV insertion site are common.
Flu-like Symptoms: Some individuals may experience fever, chills, cough, or sore throat.
Heart Rate Fluctuations: Certain medications can temporarily affect heart rate.

list.title: Allergic Reactions:
list.snippet: These can range from mild (itching, rash) to severe (difficulty breathing, swelling of lips or tongue).

list.title: Infusion Reactions:
list.snippet: These reactions can include itching, rash, flushing, fever, chills, back or belly pain, muscle or joint pain, fast heartbeat, or shortness of breath.

list.title: Infections:
list.snippet: Infusion therapy can weaken the immune system, increasing the risk of infections.

list.title: Pulmonary Edema:
list.snippet: Excess fluid in the lungs, causing shortness of breath and coughing up frothy mucus.

list.title: Air Embolism:
list.snippet: Air entering the bloodstream, causing shortness of breath, increased heart rate, and other symptoms.

text_blocks.snippet: When to Seek Immediate Medical Attention:

list.snippet: Trouble Breathing or Shortness of Breath: Seek immediate medical attention.
Chest Pain: Seek immediate medical attention.
Severe Allergic Reactions: Difficulty breathing, severe rash, or swelling.
Signs of Infection: Fever, chills, redness, or pain at the IV site.
Any other concerning or unexpected side effects:
Monitor for Symptoms: Be aware of potential side effects and report any concerns to your healthcare team promptly.
Early Reporting is Key: In many cases, side effects can be managed or reversed if reported early.
Follow Your Doctor's Instructions: Adhere to your healthcare provider's recommendations for managing side effects and post-infusion care.

text_blocks.snippet: It is crucial to discuss potential side effects with your healthcare provider before starting infusion therapy. They can help you understand the risks and benefits, and develop a plan to manage any side effects that may occur.
